name: Basic moral truths are open to human reason
plainSummary: In the Thomistic family of views, people can often know—without special revelation—that certain actions are wrong or disordered, because they bear on human flourishing and justice.
whyRoot: If some moral structure is knowable in principle, then religious and secular interlocutors can still argue about vices, virtues, and law on overlapping ground. This axiom does not deny revelation; it marks a distinct stopping point for what reason alone is said to reach.
description: Foundational claim associated with classical natural-law theory (including Thomism): core requirements of practical reason—such as prohibitions on grave injustice and certain disordered acts—are in principle accessible through reflection on human nature and the common good, not only through scripture.
